title: DC-area forecast: Rainy into this evening. Still breezy with light showers Sunday.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Showers continue into this evening with a gusty breeze and temperatures in the 50s. We could see a partial lull in the rain after midnight.

What's next? Breezes and showers may increase again by late Sunday morning, lasting through much of the afternoon. Gradually brighter skies and calmer conditions early week.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Showers, some moderate to heavy, continue into the evening before becoming more scattered and lighter by and after midnight. Breezes continue from the north, with gusts near 30 mph through early evening before easing slightly. Lows in the mid-50s to near 60. Confidence: Medium

Radar forecast for this evening

Tomorrow (Sunday): Mostly cloudy and cool, with mainly light, scattered showers, especially very late morning into at least midafternoon. Dry intervals are likely at times too. Breezy from the northwest, with a couple of gusts near 30 mph. Highs in the upper 50s to mid-60s. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Cloudy skies stick around, with a slight chance of a lingering shower. Winds stay breezy from the northwest but gradually ease. Temperatures may prove relatively steady in the mid-50s to around 60. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Skies are mostly cloudy Monday as highs reach the upper 60s to low 70s. Breezes gradually decrease. Confidence: Medium

Skies start to clear Tuesday, with a mix of sun and clouds continuing into Wednesday. Highs climb back into the mid- to upper 70s both days, with light winds around 5 to 10 mph. Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 5/10: At least the morning is dry before shower chances increase this afternoon. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for September 26

Intense late-season heat in 1930 pushed temperatures to 96 degrees, capping a brutal summer marked by persistent 90s and a historic drought.
